figures.title: How a call through a base pointer reaches the right function
figures.description: A Gradebook box holds a pointer labelled scheme_ of type GradingScheme pointer. An arrow from it points to one of two objects shown below: a PointsBased object and a Weighted object. A call written as scheme underscore arrow computePercentage leaves the Gradebook and follows the pointer. Two labelled paths show that when the pointer refers to the PointsBased object the points-based rule runs, and when it refers to the Weighted object the weighted rule runs. A note records that Gradebook contains no branch and never asks which kind it holds.
